- The "items" represent the ties being drawn from the rack.

To ensure that we have at least two ties of the same color, we need to consider the worst-case scenario where each tie picked is a different color. If there are \( m \) different colors, in the worst case, we could pick one tie of each color without having any duplicates. Once we draw one more tie, it must match one of the previously drawn ties.

Therefore, if there are 5 different colors (red, violet, blue, pink, green), in the worst-case scenario:
1. We can pick 1 red tie.
2. We can pick 1 violet tie.
3. We can pick 1 blue tie.
4. We can pick 1 pink tie.
5. We can pick 1 green tie.

At this point, we have one tie of each color (5 ties). The next tie we draw will necessarily match one of the colors already drawn. Thus, to guarantee at least two ties of the same color, we need to draw \( 5 + 1 = 6 \) ties.

This approach ensures that no matter how the ties are distributed among the different colors, drawing 6 ties guarantees that at least two will be of the same color.
